name: keep
title: Keep: Plain Words Become a Script
html:
Keep: Plain Words Become a Script

Once {watch} is answered,
  at {pr}, merge it by
  squashing `as merged`
➜
- once-answered:
    reply: watch
    steps:
      - act: scm:merge
        fields: { method: squash }
        then:
          - check: merged is true
          - keep-as: merged
At {jenkins}, build commit
  {merged.merge_commit_sha} `as build`
Once {build} is answered,
  follow its in-reply-to link
  Run the smoke script it
  links as ci:smoke-test …
➜
- ask: ci:build
  fields: { commit: ${merged.merge_commit_sha} }
  reply: build
- once-answered: { reply: build }
  - follow: hr:in-reply-to
    - run-script: ci:smoke-test
      on-link: ci:deployment
If {smoke.passed}, at {dev},
  … promote commit …, citing
  {smoke.passing} of {smoke.of}
Otherwise, at {pr}, act
  scm:comment …
➜
- given: smoke.passed is true
  then:
    - act: env:promote
      fields:
        commit: ${merged.merge_commit_sha}
        smoke: # review: the reasoner chose it
  otherwise:
    - act: scm:comment

Shortened to fit; the whole script is one click away. Inputs stay inputs: the pull request, the addresses, the book to renew.

the kept script, whole
say: Here's what artie generate kept, next to the words it came from. Once the watch is answered, merge it by squashing: that became once-answered, an act on scm:merge with method squash, and a check that it really merged. Build it and smoke-test what the build links: an ask on ci:build with a reply, a follow of the reply's in-reply-to link, and a run-script on the smoke test the build links, on the deployment it links. And the if-otherwise line became given, then, otherwise. Notice the one review mark. Citing N of M scenarios passed took judgment once; Claude shaped it into the form's smoke field, and the script says so, so a person checks it before it's kept.
